heading: NSC for NRIs: Can Non-Resident Indians Invest and Claim Tax Benefits?
tldr: Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are generally not eligible to open new National Savings Certificate (NSC) accounts.
If an individual holds an NSC account and subsequently becomes an NRI, they cannot renew it or open a new one.
For existing NSCs held by individuals who became NRIs, the account can be continued until maturity.
However, NRIs cannot claim Section 80C tax deductions for investments made in NSCs after acquiring NRI status.
The interest earned on NSC for NRIs is fully taxable in India and is generally subject to TDS.
caption:
Many NRIs wonder if they can invest in National Savings Certificates (NSC) and save on taxes. The simple answer is: generally, no, you can't open new ones. If you already have an NSC and become an NRI, you can keep it till it matures, but you won't get tax benefits anymore, and the interest is taxable. Find out exactly what this means for your money.
